# Research: Personal context

Checked on 2026-11-04 against the Claude Code CLI 2.1.318 and the Python standard library.

## R1. The block (FR-003, FR-004)

**Facts**: Claude Code reads the user's `CLAUDE.md` in its configuration directory,
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude` (the CLI's own strings name both). HTML comments are
invisible when Markdown is rendered and are kept as text.

**Decision**: the block, with `\n` newlines before it is spliced:

```text
<!-- opscout:personal-context:begin -->
<!-- Generated by opscout from your configuration: edit the configuration, then run opscout context apply. -->
## Personal context

- Answer in <language>.
- Time zone: <timezone>.

### <heading>

- <line>
<!-- opscout:personal-context:end -->
```

The language and time zone lines appear only when configured. Nothing depends on the clock,
the machine or the target, so the same configuration gives the same bytes (FR-004).

## R2. Finding and replacing the block (FR-006, FR-009)

**Revised after the independent review**: lines are split at `\n` only (not at the other
breaks `str.splitlines` knows), a byte order mark before a first-line marker is kept, a file
ending in a bare `\r` is refused before appending (the added newline would form a CRLF and
make the next run rewrite the block), and the diff marks a last line without a newline as
`diff` does, so lines never run together.

**Decision**: a line holding `opscout:personal-context:begin` or `…:end` is a marker, and it
must be exactly the marker line (a trailing `\r` aside). Exactly one begin before exactly one
end: the lines from begin to end are replaced. No marker at all: the block is appended; the
text gets a final newline if it lacks one, then a blank line, then the block. Anything else
(one marker, out of order, two blocks, a marker inside other text) is a `MarkerError` naming
the line, and nothing is written. A file holding `\r\n` gets the block with `\r\n`.

## R3. Confirmation (FR-007, FR-008; clarified 2026-11-04)

**Decision**: the code is the first 12 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the current
bytes (or a fixed marker for "no file") and the new bytes. `apply --confirm <code>`
recomputes it and writes only on a match, so a change to the file or the configuration
after the diff is refused. Without `--confirm`, apply asks `Write these changes to <path>?
[y/N]` only when standard input and output are both terminals; otherwise it prints the
diff and the code and exits 1. The code guards against a change in between, not against an
attacker: anyone who can run the command can also edit the file.

**Revised after the independent review**: after a terminal yes, the change is computed
again and written only if its code is unchanged, since Claude Code itself writes to this
file and the answer may come much later; `write()` also reads the target once more just
before the move. Codes are compared without regard to case.

**Exit codes**: diff 0 (nothing to change) or 1 (a change); apply 0 (written, or nothing to
change) or 1 (not confirmed); both 2 when they cannot run (no section, an invalid
configuration, a malformed or unreadable target).

## R4. Writing (FR-010)

**Decision**: the target is resolved through symbolic links; its directory is created when
missing; the new bytes go to a temporary file in that directory, which is flushed, given the
old file's permissions (or 0666 less the umask for a new file, as an editor would) and moved over the target with
`os.replace`, which is atomic on one file system. On any error the temporary file is
removed and the target is untouched. Targets above 1 MiB or not UTF-8 are refused before
anything is rendered into them.

## R5. Validation (FR-001, FR-002)

`timezone` must be listed by `zoneinfo.available_timezones()` exactly as written
(`Europe/Lisbon`, `UTC`; loading alone accepts a miscased name on a case-insensitive disk),
with no path characters beyond `/`; `language` is one line of 1–40 characters; up to 20 sections, each a
heading of 1–60 characters not starting with `#` and 1–50 lines of 1–300 characters; no
value holds a line break of any kind (`\n`, `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`,
U+2028, U+2029) or `opscout:personal-context`; a heading does not start with `#` or a space.
An empty section (`{}`) is refused. The generated JSON Schema states the heading pattern and
"at least one field" too, so an editor refuses what the engine refuses.
